Roles in application delivery

Scope: Because the platform’s specific workflow and governance model were not supplied, this is a general role interpretation.

AI agents: Assist with requirements analysis, design suggestions, code or configuration generation, documentation, testing, troubleshooting, and repetitive workflow automation. Their outputs require appropriate human review, permissions, and governance.
Developers: Turn requirements and designs into working software or platform configurations, integrate systems, review changes, resolve defects, and support deployment and maintenance.
Architects: Define the solution structure, technology patterns, integration boundaries, security and data approaches, nonfunctional requirements, and technical guardrails.
Testers: Develop test strategies and cases, verify functional and nonfunctional behavior, identify defects, assess release risk, and support quality automation.
Product owners: Set product goals, represent stakeholder value, prioritize the backlog, clarify acceptance criteria, make scope tradeoffs, and accept or reject completed outcomes.
Business users: Provide domain knowledge and real-world needs, review prototypes, participate in user acceptance testing, validate usability and business fit, and provide operational feedback.

Responsibility remains shared: AI agents augment delivery, while accountable people make decisions, approve changes, and validate that the application is valuable, safe, and fit for use.
limitations: Platform-specific permissions, handoffs, and role definitions cannot be confirmed from the supplied context.
